verdict.left_looks: A boxy, rounded-gable barn-like hall with a tall, nearly vertical red wall mass and white/grey stepped trim along the top edge. The facade is a red-and-white checkered front with a wooden canopy, lanterns, hay bales and barrels at the entrance. The roof is dark grey stone-brick, with an odd box-like cap on top. The side walls are plain red with a few light window recesses and a grey stone base. The back is a flat, tall red face with a stepped white parapet and a dark cap block; it reads as a flat lid over a slab.
verdict.right_looks: A pitched, stepped-gable timber-and-brick house with a brown stair-stepped roof, a clear red plaster infill with tan wood corner posts and patterned wood panels, and a grey stone plinth. The entrance has a white-framed opening with a checkered wood interior and a wood picket fence. The side walls have light window recesses and a clean stone base. The back gable is a stepped roof with a small window opening and a stone plinth, with a clear sense of a closed envelope and a readable roof.
verdict.why: The right build has a readable pitched roof with stepped gables, layered wall materials (plaster, timber posts, stone plinth) and a clearer facade, while the left reads as a flat red slab with a lid-like cap and a heavy, under-detailed roof.
